candidates.title: Weaken to Strengthen: Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Reasoning Models
candidates.content: Self-distillation offers a way to improve reasoning models when a suitable external teacher is unavailable. However, common approaches rely on privileged information to construct a stronger self-teacher, limiting their use when only unlabeled prompts are available. In this paper, we introduce Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation (WISD), which instead constructs a weaker counterpart of the original model and uses the contrast between the two as a training signal without requiring privileged information. We explore two ways to construct the weaker model: low-bit quantization and magnitude pruning. We evaluate WISD across diverse architectures and scales on mathematical and coding reasoning tasks. Across these benchmarks, quantization and pruning improve average accuracy over the original models by 4.0 and 5.5 percentage points, respectively, achieving state-of-the-art performance even without privileged information. Notably, pruning raises Qwen3.5-4B's accuracy from 57.7% to 70.5% on HMMT 2025 and from 39.1% to 56.7% on LiveCodeBench v6. Quantization raises Qwen3.6-35B-A3B's accuracy from 68.5% to 74.6% and from 61.8% to 69.5% on the same benchmarks, respectively. These resu

candidates.title: Unlocking Any-Order Generation in Pretrained Autoregressive Image Models
candidates.content: Autoregressive (AR) image generators are powerful in principle but inflexible in practice: training with a fixed raster-scan order hardcodes a single factorization of the image distribution into the model, leaving it unable to inpaint, outpaint, or edit at inference time. Existing solutions, including the modern discrete-diffusion family, train from scratch on a mixture of token orderings, paying roughly 3x the compute of standard raster-scan training; discrete diffusion further sacrifices compatibility with the AR inference ecosystem (KV caching, vLLM) by construction. We argue that this cost is unnecessary. A pretrained raster-scan AR model has already learned the joint distribution over image tokens; what it lacks is not knowledge but the ability to express that knowledge through non-sequential conditional pathways. We propose a recipe for adapting pretrained raster-scan models into any-order generators using two components: future-aware positional embeddings that resolve a target-position identifiability problem at negligible overhead, and an ordering curriculum that traces a stable optimization path from the pretrained solution to a good any-order basin. candidates.title: Broken on Arrival: Non-Functional Quantized LLM Artifacts in Public Model Registries and How to Catch Them
candidates.content: Developers download quantized large language models (LLMs) from public registries to run them locally. None of the registries we examined documented functional testing of their files. We tested all 305 eligible code-capable GGUF tags (the llama.cpp format) across 15 model lines in the official Ollama library, plus 22 popular Hugging Face community files. A 15-task code screen identified suspects, which we retested on all 164 HumanEval+ tasks. Seven official tags (2.3%) solved at most six of them. All were low-bit quantizations of models with at most four billion parameters. We rebuilt five suspect files from the original weights. All five registry files matched our uncalibrated rebuilds tensor for tensor, so none was corrupted. Exact reproducibility did not imply function. With the weights, toolchain and tensor mix held fixed, adding an importance matrix raised three Qwen2.5-Coder-3B builds from zero to 76-113 solved tasks. The same uncalibrated recipe left the smaller Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B functional, showing that the recipe alone does not predict failure. None of 66 sampled tags that passed the screen was non-functional. candidates.title: dbreunig/nesformer
candidates.content: dbreunig/nesformer Inspired by qwenputer by Divyansh Agrawal, Drew Breunig baked a working emulator for a Nintendo Entertainment System 6502 CPU into the weights of Qwen3.5-4B. You can now play NES ROMs such as Super Mario Bros (very slowly) running inside Qwen! In a comment on Hacker News Drew reveals the Opus 5.5 prompts he used to build this system: Read this article and any relevant source code: https://divagr.com/blog/qwenputer. Then explore if you could emulate the chip and ram in a Nintendo Entertainment System (as people do today with FPGAs in MISTRs) using this technique. If so, what size model would you have to build and if you could use smaller faster ones, could you get it to be at the standard clockspeed. Followed by: I think we should build it! Just for fun. It's okay if it's not fast. We want to be able to have the weights, and a cli to run them that we can point at a ROM. Apparently Opus found and then used this collection of conformance tests for the NES CPU released 15 years ago by Christopher Pow. Via Hacker News Tags: games , ai , generative-ai , llms , drew-breunig , qwen , conformance-suites

candidates.title: Quoting Ted Sanders
candidates.content: In general, LLM performance is incredibly multidimensional. There's no guarantee of a fixed ordering where the model that is best at math is also the model that's best at jokes. Despite that complexity, much of the variation in performance is explained by just a single variable: model size. In general, models that are bigger will (a) be more performant / reliable, (b) cost more per token, and (c) have better recall of esoteric facts. As you note, our models are ordered: Luna < Terra < Sol < Astra [ ... ] These days, version number signifies a few things at once: the order of release, the relationship to other releases, and the magnitude of improvement. So something like 6.1 would indicate it was launched after 5.6, may share some similarities to other 6.1 models in terms of training data / personality (which is why it's not 5.7), and isn't a giant enough leap to merit the headlines and expectations that would come with a 7. — Ted Sanders , explaining OpenAI's model naming conventions Tags: generative-ai , gpt , openai , ai , llms , ted-sanders

candidates.title: Data analysis of experimentally solved nucleosome arrays reveals heterogeneous features
candidates.content: Abstract Atomic-resolution nucleosome array structures have provided invaluable information on eukaryotic genome packing. Although these arrays are often obtained for regular fibers with designed sequences, such information complements in vivo genome organization data and modeling studies. Here, we analyze such systems with a focus on chromatin organization. We highlight both robust and unique features, as well as suitable average values for coarse-grained modeling, such as the relative orientation and positioning of neighboring nucleosomes, and opening of the linker DNA. Our associated web resource (https://www.biomath.nyu.edu/chromstruct/) shares these collected systems and provides tools for their analysis. The heterogeneous features exhibit a wide range of geometrical properties that depend on linker DNA length, core histone protein variants, auxiliary protein binding, and fiber interdigitation. Yet experimental fiber geometries can be reproduced reasonably using average parameters, as demonstrated here by simulations with our mesoscale model for regular fibers and as reported separately for life-like systems with epigenetic marks. candidates.title: Structural probing of RNA hairpins quantifies protein occupancy on RNA and links it to function in human cells
candidates.content: Abstract RNA structures that form inside living cells govern processes ranging from translation to RNA decay, many of which are controlled by RNA-binding proteins (RBPs). Because RBP specificity can depend on both RNA sequence and folding, traditional pulldown-based methods often obscure the structural context of bound RNAs. Here, a quantitative framework based on dimethyl sulfate mutational profiling and sequencing was established to directly measure RNA structure and RBP binding in human cells at single-nucleotide resolution. Applied to a 1600-member MS2 hairpin library, this approach revealed that RNA folding is the strongest determinant of MS2 coat protein (MCP) recognition in the MS2–MCP system, requiring formation of a stable hairpin and a consensus loop sequence, with stem length or GC content contributing primarily through their effect on hairpin folding. An in-cell occupancy model was derived to quantify fractional binding from structural readouts. candidates.title: The HELLS–MCM5 axis coordinates transcription–replication dynamics to preserve genomic integrity in ALK-negative anaplastic large cell lymphoma
candidates.content: Abstract The chromatin remodeler HELLS acts as a pleiotropic guardian of genomic integrity, orchestrating critical processes from DNA replication to DNA damage repair. In anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALCL), HELLS functions as a transcriptional sentinel, fine-tuning chromatin accessibility and RNA polymerase II kinetics to sustain the oncogenic transcriptional landscape essential for lymphomagenesis. Here we show that HELLS preserves genomic stability and sustains ALK-negative ALCL proliferation by preventing transcription–replication conflicts. HELLS acts as a global regulator of R-loop homeostasis while transcriptionally sustaining MCM5, a core subunit of the replicative MCM2–7 complex, which locally restrains replication-transcription collisions at actively transcribed loci. Mechanistically, HELLS loss reduces MCM5 levels, triggering aberrant firing of origins within transcriptionally active regions and consequent collisions between replication forks and the transcription machinery. Being positioned distally from R-loop-enriched sites, HELLS and MCM5 cooperate to preserve genome integrity, with MCM5 acting as the effector that delivers locus-specific protection against replica

candidates.title: E. coli-produced nanobody fusions as a pan-serotype platform for AAV purification, quantification, and detection
candidates.content: Research, production and application of the recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) require versatile tools for rapid and cost-effective advances. We developed fusion constructs with the pan-serotype, AAV-binding VHH-antibody-fragment named nanobody AAVX and devised procedures for AAV purification, quantification, and detection. Starting from an amino acid sequence, we cytosolically expressed in E. coli nanobody AAVX carrying various tags and fusion partners. Very efficient soluble production followed by a one-step immobilized metal-ion affinity chromatography (IMAC) yielded mostly >90% pure protein. Crosslinking AAVX with an agarose matrix enabled efficient purification of intact AAV2 and AAV5 capsids from cell lysates, as assessed by qPCR and ELISA. AAVX also supported effective AAV quantification by ELISA, as capture reagent and, when fused to luciferase, as detection reagent. Using tagged AAVX and streptavidin biosensors, we developed a rapid and label-free quantification assay of AAV capsids by biolayer interferometry (BLI). candidates.title: Building synthetic cell-cell synapses using engineered scaffold protein condensates
candidates.content: Synaptic assemblies that form at cell-cell junctions are often organized by multivalent scaffold proteins with condensate forming properties. An emerging hypothesis is that these scaffolds provide a thresholding mechanism whereby small increases in the density of cell-cell recognition receptors can trigger all-or-none assembly selectively at the correct partner cell interface. We test this hypothesis by engineering synthetic scaffolded synapses. Coarse-grained simulations suggest that properly-tuned scaffold interactions can yield a sharp condensation threshold. Guided by these simulations, we designed modular scaffold proteins consisting of PDZ domains and intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) of different molecular grammars. Within a specific region of parameter space, controlled by valency, receptor binding affinity and IDR-driven condensation, the synthetic scaffold proteins exhibit switch-like condensation behaviors, where co-condensates of receptor and scaffold selectively form only at interfaces with the proper partner cell. candidates.title: Duality Vaccination through Nanodesign of Click-Ligated B-Cell Inhibitory Receptor Bridging
candidates.content: Synthesis of precise and robust molecular architectures is critical to harness the power of the immune system. The dimensions, rigidity and multivalency of nanoparticles contribute to eliciting high levels of antibodies from vaccination. However, antibodies vary hugely in quality: some antibodies are highly effective at neutralizing pathogens, while others provide little or no benefit. Here we establish switchable and modular platforms for protein and nanoparticle assembly that program the target of antibody responses. We introduce Duality vaccination: the simultaneous delivery of activating and inhibitory stimuli for focusing immune responses. To construct activatory immunogens, we employ click biology with spontaneous amidation to functionalize plug-and-display self-assembling porous dodecahedral nanocages. We construct inhibitory immunogens using SpyMask protease-gated bispecific assembly, ligating the antigen to binders that bridge the B cell receptor to immune checkpoint receptors. candidates.title: EWSR1 associates with the 40S ribosomal subunit and represses translation to maintain endoplasmic reticulum homeostasis
candidates.content: Abstract FET family proteins (FUS, EWSR1, and TAF15) have garnered significant attention due to their involvement in oncogenic fusions and mutations in various cancers and neurodegenerative disorders. Although these highly conserved RNA-binding proteins are widely described as multifunctional regulators of gene expression, their precise molecular functions remain incompletely understood. Here, we uncover a previously unrecognized role for EWSR1 as a selective translational repressor in cancer cells. EWSR1 specifically targets mRNAs involved in lipid metabolism and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis. Loss of EWSR1 disrupts ER morphology and impairs activation of the unfolded protein response of the ER (UPR ER ). Mechanistically, EWSR1 represses translation upon association with target mRNAs, and its conserved region spanning two arginine–glycine–glycine (RGG) boxes contributes to association with the 40S ribosomal subunit. These findings define a novel role for EWSR1 in post-transcriptional gene regulation and suggest that perturbations in its translational activity may underlie the pathogenesis of FET-associated diseases.

candidates.title: Foundation models unlock robust phenotypic representations from Cell Painting images
candidates.content: Nature Methods, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03271-y We pretrained and systematically benchmarked a suite of self-supervised foundation models on the largest public Cell Painting dataset, enabling robust morphological feature extraction directly from multichannel high-content images without cell segmentation or feature engineering. These models outperformed classical methods and demonstrated generalizability across cell types.

candidates.title: Multivalent ADAR1 recruitment for precise RNA editing
candidates.content: Nature Methods, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03285-6 Current ADAR-recruiting RNA editing systems suffer from limited efficacy and bystander editing. We developed a system in which the multivalent recruitment of endogenous ADAR1 p150 through its Zα domain enables up to 100% A-to-I editing in vitro and 84% in vivo, enabling precise correction of disease-associated mutations at the transcript level.

candidates.title: Continuous mass measurement of single proteins
candidates.content: Nature Methods, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03275-8 We developed an approach to monitor the mass of individual proteins and the complexes they form for up to an hour by mass photometry. The ability to follow the mass of individual species enables the detection and characterization of interactions as a function of time — the essence of biomolecular mechanisms.

candidates.title: Reasoning or Pattern Exploitation? Mechanistic Insights from RL-Trained Language Models
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.39182v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly described as acquiring "reasoning" skills after reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. However, whether these gains reflect genuine reasoning or more superficial adaptations remains underexplored. In this work, we probe LLMs trained in a finite and exhaustively analyzable logical domain, namely Tic-Tac-Toe, and trace how internal representations evolve across reinforcement learning (RL) with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Quantitatively, RL yields high accuracy and robustness across prompt variations, suggesting the emergence of game reasoning. Mechanistic interpretability, however, paints a different picture: features extracted with sparse autoencoders (SAEs) reveal that models primarily adapt to rely more heavily on information already explicit in the prompt, such as whose turn it is, game progression and board occupancy. In comparison, high-level concepts like board symmetries and strategic forks remain weakly represented, raising concerns that reasoning benchmarks overestimate model abilities. candidates.title: PsychoSafe: Eliciting Psychologically-Informed Refusals in Large Language Models
candidates.content: arXiv:2606.09697v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) routinely face requests that should be refused, creating a trade-off between helpfulness and harm prevention. However, refusals themselves can be helpful. In high-risk interactions involving crisis, coercion, or escalating intent, blunt non-compliance may prevent direct harm while still failing to support the needs of the person behind the request. We present PsychoSafe, a psychologically-informed refusal framework that reframes refusal as structured supportive communication grounded in evidence-based intervention strategies. To develop PsychoSafe, we construct a corpus of 8,019 prompt-response pairs spanning five psychologically salient risk domains and apply prompting and parameter-efficient fine-tuning to Qwen 3.5 27B. On a balanced validation set of 500 prompts, evaluated with an LLM judge and validated through human ratings, PsychoSafe prompting improves overall refusal quality by 28.1% over a generic baseline, with particularly strong gains in external resource referral (+46.8%) and psychological grounding (+34.8%), while preserving downstream performance on non-refusal tasks. candidates.title: When Charts Deceive Web Agents: A Paired Benchmark for Misleading Visualization-Grounded Tasks
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.12823v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Web agents increasingly browse, interpret, and act on web content on behalf of users. In many realistic workflows, however, the visual evidence they consume is not neutral: charts and dashboards can be misleading, shaping judgments without issuing any explicit malicious instruction. Unlike chart question answering, Web Agents treat charts as intermediate evidence whose misinterpretation can propagate into concrete downstream actions --- a reliability risk that remains underexplored. We introduce MisVisAgentBench, the first paired executable benchmark for evaluating how misleading visualizations affect Web Agent execution. It comprises 280 task instances in matched clean--misleading pairs that differ only in chart evidence. We further provide a diagnostic framework that isolates misleading-induced failures from baseline task difficulty and captures execution-level effects such as extra browsing steps and decision hesitation. Across thirteen vision-language Web Agents, replacing clean charts with misleading counterparts reduces the average task success rate by more than 34 percentage points. candidates.title: FilingLoop: Evaluating and Evolving LLM Agents for Corporate Disclosure Review and Revision
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.37905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public disclosure repositories such as SEC EDGAR support informed investment through web access to corporate filings. Supporting their review with language model agents requires discovering unstated deficiencies across related documents, acquiring missing company facts, and verifying that requested revisions satisfy evidence-backed requirements. Existing financial question-answering evaluations provide limited evidence of these interactive capabilities. We introduce \textbf{FilingLoop}, an interactive benchmark and a self-evolving agent framework for corporate disclosure review and revision. Grounded in historical U.S.\ Securities and Exchange Commission correspondence, FilingLoop reconstructs 380 predominantly IPO review tasks from 96 companies under distinct information constraints. An evaluator separate from the acting agents scores final filings and responses against 6,099 eligible requirements and audits unsupported claims and harmful revisions. candidates.title: Think Before You Act: Decision Gate for LLM Agents
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.38620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents increasingly perform consequential actions through external tools, yet their proposed actions are often executed without independent verification of policy compliance or task completion. We introduce JevAct, a runtime verification framework that intercepts selected agent actions before execution and enables feedback-driven correction. JevAct compiles domain policies into executable state checks and structured questions evaluated by a prefill-only decision model, which produces probability-based judgments without relying on LLM generation. By combining deterministic verification of tool-state facts with probabilistic assessment of conversational context, the framework identifies potentially invalid actions and premature task termination, providing targeted feedback for bounded revision. JevAct operates independently of the underlying agent model and requires no modifications to its parameters or tools. We evaluate JevAct across eleven LLM agents on $\tau^2$-bench Airline and Telecom tasks and BFCL. candidates.title: Dungeons & Dragons Encounter Analysis with Semi-Random Simulation in Foundry VTT
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.38975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dungeons & Dragons (D&D) is a tabletop roleplaying game (TTRPG) in which a group of players, guided by a Game Master, roleplay a fantasy adventure with simulated combat and improvisational narrative. In D&D, an encounter is a single instance of simulated combat, where the players must use their characters to attempt to defeat a selection of enemy characters that the GM controls. D&D has multiple systems that approximate encounter difficulty by summing individual difficulty values that designers predefine for each enemy. However, since players and enemies can have a wide variety of capabilities, encounter difficulty depends on more than just the estimated difficulty of each monster. For example, these metrics do not account for positioning and dungeon layout, the synergies between monster abilities, and player party composition. We have created a tool, Mage-Hand, that can simulate D&D encounters semi-randomly using Foundry Virtual Tabletop, a virtual tabletop (VTT) system. candidates.title: Beyond LLM Wrappers: Context Engineering and the Three-Engine Architecture for Reliable Financial AI
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.39230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Financial AI systems must support decision-bearing questions involving payments, collections, cash flow, and compliance while ensuring numerical accuracy, traceability, and auditability. Large language models (LLMs) enable natural language interaction but cannot independently guarantee reproducible calculations or evidence-grounded recommendations. We present a production-grounded architecture integrating three components: a financial knowledge graph for enterprise relationships, temporal context, and provenance; a deterministic optimization engine for financial calculations and decisions; and a multi-agent LLM layer for intent interpretation, task orchestration, explanation, and claim validation. A coordination layer, termed context engineering, selects, ranks, composes, and validates query-specific context across ERP systems, tools, and tenants. Based on observations from 15 deployments over approximately 11 months, single-agent pipelines exhibited hallucination rates of about 7-9% (5-10% across query types), including invented invoices and unsupported financial claims. candidates.title: From Intent to Improvement: Agentic Dataset Search for Better Model Training
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.39608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finding training data in million-scale machine learning repositories is a Web search problem where text relevance is not enough. A query couples a semantic training goal with constraints such as task, license, and training stage, and the metadata that would verify them are often missing. Text retrieval ranks dataset cards by similarity but cannot enforce hard constraints or follow the relations that reach a sparsely described dataset. Free-form tool-calling agents are more flexible, but the same model that picks a dataset also declares it a match, and nothing checks that the query's constraints are actually met. Neither approach establishes that the data it returns will improve model training. To address it, we propose AgenticDS, a contract-governed agentic framework in which every language model decision instantiates a typed object before deterministic code consumes it. candidates.title: CADENCE: Distributional Next-Transaction Forecasting for Business Cash-Flow Underwriting
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.38084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recurring cash flows are the backbone of cash-flow underwriting: they separate durable revenue from one-off deposits, expose standing obligations, and ultimately determine ability to pay. For small businesses, recurrence is both indispensable and hard to estimate, because much of their income arrives as ambiguous transfers, most payment streams are short, and schedules follow calendar conventions that frequency-domain methods treat as noise. We present CADENCE, Calendar-Aware Distributional Event Network for Cash-Flow Estimation, a compact causal Transformer that treats each transaction as a token and predicts the amount and a full, nonparametric timing distribution of every cash flow's next payment. Inheriting transaction semantics from an external labeler and a frozen text encoder keeps CADENCE compact yet general across the long tail of small-business counterparties, while predicting a calibrated distribution rather than an opaque embedding makes its outputs interpretable enough to feed existing underwriting models and power credit decisions.
